pr_body:
Motivation:

We didnt strictly validate HTTP versions while decoding.

Modifications:

- Add extra validation logic in HttpRequestDecoder / HttpResponseDecoder
- Add unit tests

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14186
pr_comments:
I don't have my computer here but iirc I have introduced encoding initial lines pooling somewhere in the stack. If we move the check down there - when a known http string is used there is no reason to check if it starts correctly, conversely it makes sense if is not a known one.
The same thing could be done by adding a stricter new HttpVersion::valueOf which has the luxury of checking among known Strings already iirc (it is another optimization I made, some time ago)
@franz1981 i think I did this now

Just tested the patch; one small note.

The original HTTP RFCs (2068 and 2616) allowed multi-digit version majors and minors. The subsequent RFCs (7230 and 9112) restricted HTTP versions to single digits.

Here's a breakdown of what other implementations do:

0. No version validation:
- OpenBSD relayd
- Mongoose
- Twisted
- Netty (before this patch)

1. Allow multi-digit version minors and majors:
- Puma
- Unicorn
- WEBrick
- Netty (assuming this patch is merged as-is)

2. Allow multi-digit minors, but require single-digit majors:
- Nginx
- Cloudflare
- Google Cloud Classic Application Load Balancer
- Envoy
- LiteSpeed

3. Require single-digit majors and minors:
- AIOHTTP
- Apache httpd
- Cheroot
- FastHTTP
- Go net/http
- Gunicorn
- H2O
- HAProxy
- Hyper
- Hypercorn
- Eclipse Jetty
- Libevent
- Libsoup
- Lighttpd
- Node.js
- Phusion Passenger
- Apache Tomcat
- Tornado
- OpenWrt uhttpd
- Uvicorn
- Waitress
- OpenBSD httpd
- Apache Traffic Server
- nghttpx
- Pingora
- Pound
- Squid
- Varnish
- Akamai GHost

Given that most implementations follow the modern version validation rules, it's probably safe to do the same in Netty.

issue_context.title: Netty doesn't sufficiently validate received HTTP versions
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. Start a Netty HTTP/1.1 server that echos the parsed components of the request, such as [this one](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/narfindustries/http-garden/main/images/netty/GardenServer.java).
2. Send it a request with an invalid version:
```sh
(printf 'POST / INVALID/12.34\r\n\r\n'; sleep 1) \
    | ncat localhost 80 \
    | grep '"version"' \
    | jq '.["version"]' \
    | xargs echo \
    | base64 -d \
    | xxd
```
3. Observe that the invalid version was not rejected, and was preserved:
```
00000000: 494e 5641 4c49 442f 3132 2e33 34         INVALID/12.34
```

### Expected behavior
The RFCs are clear that HTTP versions need to consist of only the ASCII bytes "HTTP/", followed by a single ASCII digit, a dot, and another ASCII digit. The recommended behavior upon receiving a request with an invalid version should be to reject the request and close the connection. This is what most HTTP implementations do, including AIOHTTP, Apache httpd, Cheroot, FastHTTP, Go net/http, Gunicorn, H2O, HAProxy, Hyper, Hypercorn, Jetty, Libevent, Libsoup, Lighttpd, Nginx, Node.js LiteSpeed, Passenger, Puma, Tomcat, Tornado, OpenWrt uhttpd, Unicorn, Uvicorn, Waitress, WEBrick, OpenBSD httpd, Apache Traffic Server, nghttpx, Pingora, Pound, Squid, Varnish, Akamai GHost, Cloudflare's CDN, Google Cloud Classic App. LB, and Envoy.

### Actual behavior
Netty accepts the request with the invalid version.

### Netty version
4.1 @ 3881103a01488785a6d2f78a3a80258dd848609f

### JVM version (e.g. `java -version`)
```
openjdk version "23-ea" 2024-09-17
OpenJDK Runtime Environment (build 23-ea+20-Debian-1)
OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (build 23-ea+20-Debian-1, mixed mode, sharing)
```

### OS version (e.g. `uname -a`)
```
Linux a2d83c065945 6.9.8-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 05 Jul 2024 22:11:24 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```
